rationale: The hypothesis posits that autosomal dominant intellectual developmental disorder 73 (MRD73 / TAF4-related NDD) is most easily confused with Coffin-Siris syndrome and Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome, and distinguishes them by the absence of hypoplastic fifth digits and coarse facial features. However, the available peer-reviewed literature detailing TAF4-related NDD (Janssen et al., 2022; Kennis et al., 2026; Staykova et al., 2024) places TAF4-related disorder firmly within the spectrum of TFIID-complex 'TAF-opathies' and nonspecific neurodevelopmental disorders / developmental language disorders (DLD). There is no empirical or clinical evidence in the cited cohort literature establishing Coffin-Siris syndrome or Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome as primary differential diagnoses or establishing fifth digit hypoplasia as a key differentiator.

evidence.text: TAF4-related neurodevelopmental disorder (T4NDD) was characterized in a discovery cohort of eight individuals harboring de novo putative loss-of-function variants, presenting with intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms, and was contextualized within TFIID-related disorders (TAF-opathies) rather than BAF-complex disorders.

source.title: De novo putative loss‐of‐function variants in TAF4 are associated with a neuro‐developmental disorder
source.quote: We here present a cohort of eight individuals, each carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) variants in TAF4 and expressing phenotypes consistent with a neuro-developmental disorder (NDD). Common features include intellectual disability, abnormal behavior, and facial dysmorphisms. We propose TAF4 as a novel dominant disease gene for NDD, and coin this novel disorder 'TAF4-related NDD' (T4NDD). We place T4NDD in the context of other disorders related to TFIID subunits, revealing shared features of T4NDD with other TAF-opathies.

new_directions.rationale: Evaluating systematic dysmorphology exams across expanded TAF4 cohorts will determine whether specific craniofacial or digital anomalies reliably discriminate T4NDD from other transcription factor IID-related disorders.
